Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — security gating & retention items

Hi Rachel — thanks for taking the time on Friday. As promised I'm pulling together a focused MAP that isolates the compliance gates (SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ, DPA redline, and data retention/custody) so your procurement and legal teams have clear checkpoints.

Quick context/questions so I can finalise the plan: 
- For the DPA redlines you attached in the demo (thanks), can you confirm whether HarborFin requires any escrow/long-term retention of tokens beyond 2 years? I want to make sure our standard retention tiers align.
- Do you have a hard date for contract signature target? You mentioned late July on the call — is July 26 still the target close date?
- Is EU-only processing (eu-west-1) required for all customer data, or only for EU resident end-users?

I'll draft a one-page MAP spreadsheet (owners, deliverables, dates, acceptance criteria) and share by EOD today. Hannah from our Customer Success will own evidence intake; Marcus will coordinate the legal handoff on DPA.

Best,

From: Rachel Adams <rachel.adams@harborfin.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — security gating & retention items

Thanks, Soojin — good plan. Quick answers: 
- Retention: HarborFin's baseline requirement for transaction logs is 7 years, but we can carve out token-level retention to a shorter window if there's an auditable deletion process. Our compliance team prefers to see technical controls documented before agreeing to less than 7 years.
- Close target: yes, July 26 is our preferred signature date (internal board review July 23).
- EU residency: Ideally EU-only processing for EU customers; for now assume EU residency is a requirement for any EU PII.

Attaching our preliminary DPA redlines (harborfin_dpa_redlines_v1.pdf) — legal flagged two main items: KMS control expectations and requirement for a subprocessor list that is contractually guaranteed to be updated within 5 business days.

Can you also include a short note on how Redwood separates customer keys (KMIP/KMS) and whether key material can be customer-managed in a dedicated deployment?

—Rachel
Rachel Adams
Head of Procurement, HarborFin

- EU residency: we need formal confirmation that production data for EU customers will remain in eu-west-1 and logs holding PII will be deleted/archived per retention windows. Is that achievable on Redwood Hosted or does that require Dedicated/Private?

If we can get those items by next Wednesday (2027-07-07), that should keep us on track for board review.

Looping in a quick commercial/legal plan: 

Options we can offer to meet HarborFin's commitments:
- Hosted (fastest): We can restrict processing regionally and offer contractual commitments, but customer-managed KMS is limited in hosted; retention policies can be configured but require technical attestations. Good for PoC/proof of concept only.
- Dedicated (recommended for HarborFin): Dedicated GPU pool + per-tenant KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and region pinning (eu-west-1). Provisioning lead time: ~3 weeks after contract — we can compress with a committed start date.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): Full control, but longer procurement and infra setup (6–10 weeks).

Action items for us now: 
1) Marcus to prepare DPA counter language for customer-managed KMS + subprocessor update clause by 2027-07-06.
2) Hannah to prepare SOC 2 excerpt (controls SC-5, SI-7) and SIG/CAIQ exports by 2027-07-07.
3) Soojin to confirm map upload to HubSpot and calendar kickoffs for evidence intake.

If we hit those dates we should have the board packet ready by July 21–23. Will schedule a legal triage call with HarborFin the week of July 5 if they want to go through redlines live.

—Marcus
Senior Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
